Frisbee
Seanbuilding friendships

When Sean first picked up a frisbee, he wasn’t looking for sports—he was looking for a place to belong. “I didn’t have many friends … I wasn’t particularly interested in sports, and I didn’t have a main hobby that I loved.” But frisbee became the doorway to friendship and a renewed sense of purpose.

Q: What did frisbee give you that you didn’t have before?

S: I gained friends, and a place where I felt good. After that, I started to attract other friends, and my friends also started playing with us. My family liked it too, because I was doing sports instead of sitting on my phone all day.

Q: Has the Bible shaped your journey?

S: John 16:33 is really good. Jesus said, “I have told you this, so that you might have peace in your hearts because of me. While you are in the world, you will have to suffer. But cheer up! I have defeated the world.”

When I started playing, other guys started talking about God and the Bible. Before that, I hadn’t thought about such topics, and it was like I found new meaning and new qualities.

Q: How does knowing Jesus change the way you play?

S: Sports is one way for people to be attracted to God. When people see his love on the field, they feel comfortable and enjoy the process.

Think about this:

What reasons do you have for playing sports?
How important are they to you?

How could you develop friends more intentionally in your sports?
